report.tagline: America's biggest retailer, using its 4,600 US stores as mini warehouses to deliver groceries and goods in hours.
report.simpleSummary: Walmart is the huge US supermarket and discount store chain. You can now order on its app and get groceries and household items delivered from your nearest store, often in under three hours. A Walmart+ membership makes delivery free and adds perks like fuel discounts and a streaming service. Walmart also owns most of Flipkart in India.

overview.whatItDoes: Walmart sells groceries, household goods, electronics and clothing at low prices through stores and its app. It turned its stores into delivery hubs, so an online order is picked from the shelf of a nearby store and driven to your door. It also runs a marketplace for outside sellers and a fast-growing ad business.
howItWorks: You order in the Walmart app, choosing delivery, pickup at the store, or shipping.
Store staff pick the items from shelves near you. Drivers from Spark Driver, Walmart's gig delivery app, bring them in as little as 30 minutes for an express fee.
Walmart+ members ($98 a year or $12.95 a month) get free delivery on orders over $35, plus fuel discounts and Paramount+ or Peacock.
Outside sellers list millions of extra items on Walmart Marketplace and can pay Walmart to store and ship them (Walmart Fulfillment Services).
Brands pay Walmart Connect to show ads in the app and on its Vizio smart TVs, using Walmart's shopper data.
In 2026 Walmart launched a $120 a year bundle of Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus.
overview.valueProposition: Everyday low prices on groceries with same-day delivery from a store near you. For families, it is often cheaper than Amazon for food and essentials.

Walmart+ includes fuel savings and Paramount+ or Peacock.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Orders are picked from the nearest store and delivered by Spark drivers.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Uses stores Walmart already pays for, so fast delivery is cheaper than building new warehouses. Grew over 40% in Q3 FY27.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Members order more often and stay loyal. Membership income rose 43% in Q3 FY27.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Adds hundreds of millions of items without inventory cost. Grew 49% in Q3 FY27.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: High-profit revenue that pays for cheap delivery.

steps.detail: Sees a 'Free 30-day Walmart+ trial' banner in the app.
Adds $90 of groceries, picks the 'Reorder' list of past store purchases.
Chooses a 2-hour slot today; free over $35 with the trial.
Gets alerts if an item is out and approves a substitute.
Driver leaves bags at the door with a photo.
After 30 days the trial turns into a paid $12.95 monthly plan.
Home screen shows usual items and Rollback deals.
Adds milk, bread and nappies in under 2 minutes.
Pays extra for delivery within an hour when urgent.
Uses Walmart+ fuel discount at a Walmart or Murphy station.
Applies to Walmart Marketplace with business details.
Imports listings from its Amazon catalogue.
Sends stock to Walmart Fulfillment Services for 2-day shipping badges.
Runs sponsored product ads through Walmart Connect.
Monitors on-time shipping and returns rate to stay eligible.

businessModel.summary: Walmart makes most of its money selling goods at thin margins, about 3 to 4% operating profit. Online growth adds three higher-margin layers: membership fees, marketplace commissions and advertising. Those layers help pay for fast delivery.

revenueStreams.detail: Groceries and general goods sold in stores and online, the vast majority of revenue.
Walmart+ ($98 a year) and Sam's Club fees. Membership income grew 43% in the US in Q3 FY27.
Walmart Connect ads in the app, stores and on Vizio TVs. Up 37% globally in Q3 FY27.
Usually 6 to 15% of the item price, plus fulfilment fees.
Flipkart and PhonePe in India, Walmex in Mexico, Walmart Canada and others; about $35.9 billion of sales in Q3 FY27.

businessModel.pricing: Walmart+ costs $98 a year or $12.95 a month in the US. Free delivery on orders over $35 for members; non-members pay about $7.95 to $9.95 per delivery. Express delivery under an hour costs about $10 extra. Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus bundle: $120 a year.
costDrivers: Cost of the goods themselves, the biggest cost by far
Store staff wages, including pickers for online orders
Technology and automation in distribution centres
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $100 grocery delivery for a Walmart+ member, Walmart earns about $24 gross margin on the goods. Picking costs about $5 to $8 and the driver about $7 to $10, so the order alone is close to break-even. What makes it work: the member fee (about $8 a month), ad money from brands on that order (a few dollars), and the fact that online customers spend more in total. Walmart says its US e-commerce business turned profitable in 2025.

howTheyGetUsers: Existing store shoppers moved online through pickup and app prompts
Walmart+ Assist at half price for people on SNAP and other benefits
The $120 Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus bundle
Higher-income households tempted by fast delivery; Walmart says these are its fastest-growing shopper group
whatBringsUsersBack: Free delivery over $35 makes members order more often
Fuel savings and streaming make the membership feel worth it
growth.moat: Walmart already has about 4,600 US stores near almost every American, full of groceries. Using them as delivery hubs gives fast delivery without building new warehouses. Its huge buying power keeps prices low. Rivals like Amazon must build fresh food networks from scratch.

competitors.name: Amazon
competitors.positioning: Largest online retailer, Prime at $139 a year with fast shipping and video.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Walmart is stronger in groceries and in rural areas, and Walmart+ is cheaper. Amazon has more items and stronger video.

competitors.name: Costco
competitors.positioning: Membership warehouse with bulk low prices.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Walmart offers smaller basket sizes and same-day delivery; Sam's Club is its Costco rival.

competitors.name: Target
competitors.positioning: Slightly more upmarket general store with Target Circle 360.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Walmart has lower prices and bigger grocery range.

competitors.name: Instacart and DoorDash
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Walmart owns the stock and the stores, so it controls price and availability.

competitors.name: Kroger
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Walmart has wider general merchandise and a bigger ad and marketplace business.

northStar.metric: Weekly households receiving an online order on time and complete
northStar.why: It captures how many families Walmart actually saves time for each week, and it only grows if orders are fast and correct. Habits form when a family relies on Walmart for every weekly shop.

guardrailMetrics: In-store availability for walk-in shoppers (online picking must not empty shelves)
Ad load in search results, so shoppers still find the cheapest relevant item
Customer complaints about missing or wrong items

Lowest grocery prices among big US chains
Fast-growing, high-margin ads and membership income
Huge cash flow to fund automation and price cuts
Owns Flipkart, a leader in Indian e-commerce

improvementIdeas.idea: Live in-stock check at the picking store before checkout, with a clear 'likely out of stock' flag and preferred swap choice.
improvementIdeas.problem: Customers get surprise substitutions or missing items.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer complaints and refunds, more trust in delivery.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show members a monthly 'you saved $X with Walmart+' summary including delivery, fuel and streaming.
improvementIdeas.problem: Members feel Walmart+ is weaker than Prime and cancel.

improvementIdeas.idea: Seller quality score that hides poorly rated marketplace sellers from top search spots.
improvementIdeas.problem: Marketplace items that do not match listings hurt Walmart's brand.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower return rates on marketplace items.

improvementIdeas.idea: Delivery photo verification with GPS check and a one-tap 'not my door' report.
improvementIdeas.problem: Orders left at the wrong address.

pmLessons: Use assets you already have. Walmart turned stores into warehouses instead of copying Amazon's network.
Thin-margin businesses can win online by adding high-margin layers like ads and memberships on top of each order.
A cheaper membership can win if it targets the most frequent need, here weekly groceries.
Speed is a product feature. Under-3-hour delivery changed how often families order.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Walmart+ against Amazon Prime?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a segment (families, rural, benefit users). Find why they do not join or why they cancel. Propose features or bundles. Track trial-to-paid and retention.

interviewQuestions.question: Walmart's store-fulfilled delivery grew 40%. What could go wrong for in-store shoppers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think empty shelves, crowded aisles from pickers, staff stress. Suggest guardrail metrics and fixes like dedicated picking hours or backroom stock.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Walmart decide how many ads to show in search?
interviewQuestions.hint: Balance ad revenue versus conversion and trust. Run A/B tests with different ad loads, measure revenue per search and repeat purchase.

interviewQuestions.question: Design an improved substitution experience.
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the journey: out-of-stock found, choice offered, customer response. Ideas: preferences at add-to-cart, AI suggestions, refunds. Metric: acceptance rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star for Walmart's online business, and why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Value delivered, not revenue. Suggest weekly households with on-time complete orders. Break into households, frequency and quality.

Per-order picking and delivery costs in the unit economics example are rough estimates, not company figures.
